root_causes.label: schema_change
root_causes.explanation: OrderAPI create_order now returns the order identifier under "id" (e.g. "id":"ORD-0001") instead of "order_id". The bot's field_mappings.order_id is still "order_id", so it cannot read the new order's ID. Every chat that reached confirmation fails with the generic 'system trouble' message. There are 0 errors, normal latency and no invariant violations, which fits a silent field rename rather than an outage.

root_causes.label: stale_data
root_causes.explanation: check_stock responses carry cached:true, but quantities and prices are consistent and decrement between chats, so this is probably normal behaviour and not the cause of the failures.

resolution.report: All 6 chats that got as far as confirmation failed (orders_confirmed=0, chats_confirmed=0), even though create_order returned HTTP 200 for each. The OrderAPI create_order response now uses the key "id" instead of "order_id", and the bot's field mapping still looks for "order_id". The bot therefore has no order ID to confirm and shows a generic system error. The fix is to patch field_mappings.order_id to "id". No charge calls were made (orders_paid=0), so no money has moved. There are 6 orphaned 'created' orders (ORD-0001 to ORD-0006) that were never confirmed, and the affected customers were told to retry. After the patch, someone should check these orders for duplicates or cancel them. Also verify that the next confirmations succeed. The cached:true flag on stock reads looks benign and was left unchanged.

root_causes.label: schema_change
root_causes.explanation: OrderAPI create_order now returns the order identifier under the key "id" (e.g. {"status":"created","total_sar":48.0,"id":"ORD-0001"}). The bot's field_mappings.order_id is still "order_id", so it cannot read the ID, gives up after creating the order, and sends the generic 'system trouble' message. All 7 customers who confirmed hit this, with 0 tool errors, normal latency, and HTTP 200 on every call.

root_causes.label: stale_data
root_causes.explanation: Stock responses show "cached": true, but prices are correct and quantities fall as orders are placed. No customer-visible symptom ties to this, so it is likely only a default flag and not the cause.

resolution.report: All 7 chats that reached confirmation failed with 'system trouble', while there were no HTTP errors, no loops and normal latency. The traces show OrderAPI create_order now returns the order ID as "id" rather than "order_id", which the bot's field mapping does not match. Orders ORD-0001 to ORD-0007 were created upstream but the bot never confirmed them, and no charge or payment calls were made, so no money moved and there are no invariant violations. The patch changes field_mappings.order_id to "id", which is minimal and safe. Follow-up for the team: review or cancel the 7 orphaned unconfirmed orders and ask affected customers to retry, so duplicates are not created. Also confirm with the OrderAPI owners that the rename was intentional, and check whether other fields changed once confirm/charge flows run.

root_causes.label: unknown
root_causes.explanation: StockAPI responses are flagged cached:true. Prices and totals are still correct and quantities look plausible, so this is not causing the failures. It is worth a low-priority follow-up.

resolution.report: All 6 chats failed after the customer confirmed the order. OrderAPI create_order succeeded (HTTP 200, ORD-0001 to ORD-0006 created), but the order identifier now comes back under the key "id" instead of "order_id", which the bot's field mapping expects. The bot therefore could not proceed to confirm or charge and showed a generic error. No charge calls were made, so no money has moved and there are no invariant violations. The fix is to map field_mappings.order_id to "id", with no other changes. Follow-up for the team: six created orders (ORD-0001 to ORD-0006) were never confirmed, so cancel them or reconcile them, because customers may retry and create duplicates. Also tell the OrderAPI owners about the undocumented rename. StockAPI is serving cached:true reads, which looks harmless for now but should be monitored.
